If you are truly looking for an old restaurant,
It is a place so suitable that it cannot be replaced.

The original Mapo Shell House. I visited this place this spring and liked it so much that I decided to visit again in the winter. The ventilation is poor and there is a lot of dust, but all of these become components that create a unique atmosphere for this space.
The biggest advantage of this place is grilling meat and fish together, so I ordered pork ribs, my favorite meat menu, and grilled fish, grilled fish. The pork ribs, heavily seasoned, were grilled just enough to keep the moisture from escaping and eaten wrapped in wraps or served over rice. When you are not busy, the early seasoned fish is served cooked at least 80%, so if you bring it to us, you can cook it a little more on the grill to suit your taste. Properly grilled clams have a good flavor and are delicious eaten on their own or served with white rice. As its name suggests, the skin is also delicious. It has a soft and chewy texture and a savory taste when dipped in soybean powder.
It's one of the first places that comes to mind when a cold wind blows at the tip of your nose. I'll have to stop by one more time before spring comes.

Yangsando Gongdeok Branch is located about a 5-minute walk from Exit 1 of Gongdeok Station. It is very easy to find the way, and since it is located within the Gongdeok Park Xi building, there is ample parking space, making it ideal for visiting by car.

reviews.text:
Izakaya ‘Sushibok’ located near Gongdeok Station
I saw this place on the internet and thought it looked good so I visited it. I don't think it's very famous yet, but I think it will become famous soon.

First of all, there are 6-8 counter seats inside the store and there are also table seats. I prefer counter seats, so I sat at the counter. Since the store opened not long ago, it was very clean.
On this day, I ordered Sashimi Moriawase for 2 (3.5), Uni Chuga (2.2), and Chicken Karaage (0.7) and felt that it was excellent value for money.
The sashimi was well prepared and fresh. The ripeness was just right. And when I visited Sushi Bok's Instagram, it seemed like the owner worked very hard to prepare the ingredients and used good ingredients.
The chicken karaage was also crispy and delicious.
Originally, I wanted to order fried abalone intestine fried noodles after eating sashimi, but I couldn't order because the ingredients were sold out.
It is said that a limited quantity of stir-fried abalone intestine noodles is sold every day, so if you want to try it, it is best to order in advance.

And it was nice that my favorite Gyeongju Beopju was sold here. Of course, we also sell soju.
When I ordered from the menu, they provided salad, soup, and beef noodles, so I was able to eat comfortably.
I think this is a restaurant that offers both great taste and value for money. However, it is a bit disappointing that it is only open until 10pm. I think it would be nice if it were open until 12 o'clock so I could make a second visit.

reviews.text: The three of us went and ordered the sashimi set for three and seaweed sushi, and all of the menu items were delicious. Even the konjac served as a basic side dish was delicious. reviews.author: Minhan Cho
reviews.text:
I really want sushi, but if you want sashimi, this is the place to go.

There is something to be said about hospitality.

Special sushi costs 25,000 won, and this is the price range where low-priced omakase is gradually appearing. I asked to change the sushi to raw fish instead of beef, and they said I couldn't change the composition unless I was allergic. Even the crappy sushi in college that costs 10,000 won per plate is usually accepted if it's common sense to ask for this and add that, but this place has a policy that makes it hard to understand whether the chef is busy or just annoying.

Additionally, customers cannot know the detailed fish species. The menu says 12pcs, and if you count the fish species included, there are 9 species. The remaining 3 points are kept secret until the food is received. Also, when it comes to sushi, you can tell the species of fish by looking at it, but I think the customer should know whether the tuna is from Spain or Mexico, where the uni is from, and what part of the beef it is. If it varies depending on the supply of ingredients every day, I think the employee should at least explain. Moreover, indicating the country of origin is also mandatory. However, it was disappointing that such efforts were not clearly visible.

First of all, the special sushi was delicious overall, but I honestly wondered if Shari and Neta were a good match for the flounder fin. The flounder was tough, probably because it was undercooked, and it was disappointing that both the flounder and flounder fin were eaten first, and the neta took a long time to chew in the mouth. The squid was slightly curled on the outside, but it was a bit thicker so I thought it would have been nice to have a sheath. In addition, the scallops, shrimp, sea urchin, and conger eel were very delicious. The conger eel was so chewy that I thought I would order anagodon separately later.

Udon and soybean soup are served before and after the sushi. The udon is commercially available and has nothing special, but the broth has a slightly sweet scent like mirin, and the soybean soup seems to be made from crab or clam.

The other day, I ate anago-don, sake-don, and futomaki banjul packaged, and they were all good. At this price and this level, accessibility is not bad.

Anyway, the sushi seems a bit long, and it seems worth visiting to eat sashimi.

I had a second year-end gathering with my friends at 'Orossilbi'.
I was very satisfied with the atmosphere and taste!

We ordered Tomato Kaisen Nabe and Butagakuni as our main menu.
The nabe broth was so delicious that it captured the coolness of the seafood and the freshness of the tomatoes at the same time. Be sure to add the raw noodles and enjoy it! (A real delicacy!)
Butagakuni was also gently simmered in a special sauce, making it the perfect accompaniment to drinks.
It's great for enjoying fusion Japanese cuisine in a simple way, so it's recommended for a date or a small gathering with friends!

I ate nanjawansu, lamb skin, yulingi, and Sichuan sweet and sour pork.
Nanjawan's seems to be a little lacking compared to the menus of regular or high-end restaurants, but it is a menu that is fully appealing due to its price.
Most recommended. Nanjawansu is generally an expensive and small portion to order, but the fact that you can taste it at this price is attractive enough, even considering the lack of taste.
Yuringi also fried the chicken until it was crispy enough, so the crunchy texture goes well with the sauce. I don't know about the other menu items, but the nanjawan and yulingi were quite good. To be honest, the other menu items were SOSO.

I don't know about the employees(?), but the owner is quite friendly.
The rice cakes shared by our neighbors were shared with us as a service. I added one star because I felt friendly.
Not bad for a second meal after eating nearby. Good for 1st drive.

Actually, this house doesn't have a large interior design, so it's not a real old restaurant.

reviews.author: Jason Ham
reviews.text:
A unique Chinese restaurant located across from the Korean Senior Citizens’ Association building on the one-way street of Imjeong-ro, west of Hyochang Park.

Regardless of whether it is a weekday or a weekend, there is always a line of visitors, but the store, which has three 4-person seats and one 2-person seat, remains the same. The reason there is a waiting line is not only because of the narrow store, but also because the speed at which the owner serves food is always constant. You can say 'the service speed is slow', but if you don't like that, don't go.

Sweet and sour pork and soybean paste are the main menu items, but the taste and aroma are different from those at common Chinese restaurants in the neighborhood. That's why I added the expression 'unique'. I can't visit it often because it's not easily accessible and there's always a waiting line, but it's a place that comes to mind every now and then.

# Closed from February 5 to March 8, 2026 due to personal reasons of the owner.

reviews.author: Traveller Jun
reviews.text:
since1981.

Ordered soy sauce and sweet and sour pork. Ganjjajang is made with finely chopped onions and the sauce mixes well. Chunjang, which has almost no sweetness, has a natural bitterness and savory taste, so it has a boring charm, but when you try it for the first time, its boringness is quite shocking. The hand-made noodles have a good texture due to their bumpy thickness. The sweet and sour pork is fried in large chunks like fried peppers and cut into pieces with scissors. Goes well with sweet sauce. Overall, a simple taste that is faithful to the original taste of the ingredients rather than a fancy taste.

I enjoyed the meal~

reviews.author: Uncold
reviews.text:
💌Dear Father,

If I get the chance, I want to take my father to an old Chinese restaurant near Hyochang Park that is famous for soybean paste.

I usually go when it opens on Saturdays, but there aren't many seats inside, so if there are about 10 people in front of me, I have to wait for more than 40 minutes. (It's difficult to get there because of the waiting time.)

The menu here is very simple. There are only 4 menu items: Ganjjajang, Jjajangmyeon, Sweet and Sour Pork, and Grilled Dumplings. Among these, soybean paste is the most famous. The black bean sauce is made by frying coarsely chopped onions together, combining umami and sweetness, and adding a refreshing touch with chives. It is very delicious. And the noodles are handmade, so when you sit down and wait, you can hear the sound of noodles being made. This is also really strange, isn't it? The noodles are all different thicknesses, so sometimes some are thicker than kalguksu, but I like being able to taste a variety of textures. The taste of the noodles is also different from other places, so when the soybean paste is served, I recommend trying the unique taste of the noodles first.

If you are expecting spicy black bean paste, you may be disappointed, and some people leave negative reviews saying that it is not tasty, but when I eat jjajangmyeon, I always have trouble digesting it and the smell of burp is bad, but this place makes my stomach feel comfortable. I wonder what my father's reaction will be. Haha

P.S There are a lot of things I regret.
1. In today’s world, card payments are not accepted.
2. Everyone who eats soy sauce needs a spoon, but it is not in the cutlery container, so you have to request it separately.
3. I was appalled by the pickled radish rehash. I never eat pickled radish here. Ugh!
4. There is a big difference in taste, but I am just thankful that it is still in operation.

💭A place that comes to mind
- Baekgaekdo in Busan, a business with as much guts as Shinseonggak, whose strong salty taste keeps coming to mind.
- Hongneunggak in Cheongnyangni, a curious place I haven’t been to yet

reviews.author: Jaebong Jang
reviews.text:
Om Restaurant is located a 3-minute walk from Exit 1 of Gongdeok Station. Although it is introduced as an Indian restaurant, it is actually a Nepalese restaurant. The menu is almost similar to Indian food, but I understand that there is also a menu unique to Nepal.
It is run by CEO K.P. Sitoula, who serves as the head of the Nepal Tourism Board, so the interior is quite luxurious, and the interior decoration that seems to have been transported to Nepal and the friendly local Nepalese employees make you forget about Korea for a moment.
Important food ingredients are sourced from Nepal, and the taste of the dishes also reflects the special features of Nepalese and Indian food.
The main one among them is the price range. While the prices of most Indian restaurants are a bit high, Om Restaurant here is really good value for money.
The spacious hall and delicious food are good for families dining out, but it also seems to be a perfect place for office workers to have a company dinner.
It would be nice to stop by when you have time.
The parking lot is also prepared, which is the icing on the cake~^^
